gloss: oracle; divine message; revelation from a god

definitions.gloss: oracle; divine message; revelation from a god
definitions.explanation: A message believed to come from a deity, delivered through a medium, priest, or other intermediary. Refers both to the message itself and to the act of receiving such a message.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}ギリシャでは{神託|しんたく}が{政治|せいじ}にも{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: In ancient Greece, oracles influenced politics as well.

examples.japanese: {王|おう}は{戦|いくさ}を{始|はじ}める{前|まえ}に{神託|しんたく}を{求|もと}め、{神官|しんかん}の{言葉|ことば}に{従|したが}った。
examples.english: The king sought a divine oracle before starting the war and followed the words of the priest.

notes:
Composed of {神|しん} (god, deity) and {託|たく} (to entrust, to commission). Frequently encountered in discussions of ancient Greek religion (the Oracle at Delphi), the Bible, and Japanese mythology.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神託|しんたく}を{受|う}ける: to receive an oracle
- {神託|しんたく}を{求|もと}める: to seek a divine message
- {神託|しんたく}を{下|くだ}す: to deliver an oracle (from a god's perspective)
- {神託|しんたく}に{従|したが}う: to follow a divine oracle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {託宣|たくせん}: oracle; divine proclamation — close synonym, slightly more formal
- お{告|つ}げ: divine revelation; message from heaven — more colloquial, used in everyday Japanese
- {啓示|けいじ}: revelation; divine disclosure — specifically the Christian concept
- {予言|よげん}: prophecy; prediction — broader, not necessarily from a deity

Do not confuse with {信託|しんたく} (trust, as in financial trust), which is a homophone with different kanji.
